business_problem: Luftfartsverket needed a way to increase air-traffic capacity and reduce pressure on controllers without compromising safety, because growing flight volumes make manual conflict management more stressful, expensive, and operationally constrained.
solution_summary: Luftfartsverket worked with IBM Garage, IBM Research, and IBM Streams engineers to build Advanced Autoplanner (AAP), a concept for autonomous air traffic control. The architecture continuously forecasts aircraft positions with a lattice-based 3D space-exploration approach, tests hundreds of possible course, speed, or altitude changes, and ranks safe instructions with a rule-based layer before presenting the best option to the pilot. Because secure production data could not be accessed remotely during the pandemic, the team connected the NLR Air Traffic Control Research Simulator (NARSIM) to IBM Streams on IBM Cloud and trained a deterministic custom algorithm against simulated traffic instead. IBM Db2 stores operational data for the Streams application, while IBM Cloudant stores instructions issued by the AAP workflow. This stack turns airspace data into conflict-resolution recommendations fast enough for real-time traffic-management experiments above normal sector loads.

solution_components.name: IBM Streams
solution_components.role: Runs the real-time analytics and conflict-resolution algorithm that forecasts aircraft trajectories and evaluates alternate actions.

solution_components.name: IBM Cloud
solution_components.role: Hosts the Streams-based AAP environment that was connected to the NARSIM simulator during development and testing.

solution_components.name: IBM Db2
solution_components.role: Stores application data for the IBM Streams-based autonomous air-traffic-control workflow.

solution_components.name: IBM Cloudant
solution_components.role: Stores the instructions that AAP sends for controllers and pilots to execute.

data_flow: Simulated air-traffic data from NARSIM is streamed into IBM Streams on IBM Cloud, where the AAP algorithm forecasts aircraft positions, tests nearly 800 alternate conflict resolutions, stores application state in Db2, records instructions in Cloudant, and presents the safest next action for pilots to execute.
integration_points: NLR Air Traffic Control Research Simulator (NARSIM)
business_outcome: LFV proved that an autonomous control concept can maintain safe aircraft separation at much higher traffic volumes, establishing a foundation for future efficiency gains and reduced controller burden in aviation operations.
metrics: solution maintains separation in air traffic control simulations at approximately 200% the normal capacity
in a single second, the app can run nearly 800 alternate conflict resolutions
first MVP in only four months
architecture_clues: AAP uses a six-nautical-mile buffer even though the aviation standard cited in the story is five nautical miles.
The workflow has two phases: 3D conflict exploration followed by rule-based ranking of safe actions.
The team trained against NARSIM because secure LFV production data could not be accessed remotely during lockdown.
